DUROFLEX — VISUAL EVIDENCE INDEX
12 October 2026

Astra (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning) returned an individual visual observation for all 371 supplied images across 11 bounded requests: 151 draft Visual World Guide slides, 106 visible Strategic Blueprint slides, 58 unique Archive.zip interior references and 56 selected current website images from 12 official pages. All 266 deck slides also supplied indexed text; nine hidden positioning slides are text only. The synthesis used these completed reviews and source text, not a second image inspection. This is model analysis, not human approval, product validation or model-weight training. Rendered deck pages may have font substitutions; embedded small images have lower detail. Videos, full social feeds and inaccessible advertising evidence remain unreviewed.
This index is assistant/model interpretation; source precedence from the companion deep research applies. Do not infer product claims from reference images.

supplied-draft-visual-guide-1
Coverage: V001, V002, V003, V004, V005, V006, V007, V008, V009, V010, V011, V012, V013, V014, V015, V016, V017, V018, V019, V020, V021, V022, V023, V024, V025, V026, V027, V028, V029, V030, V031, V032, V033, V034, V035, V036, V037, V038
Reviewed all 38 supplied images individually. The draft proposes a coherent Duroflex world built through warm architectural surfaces, directional daylight, tactile detail, supported leisure and restrained brand red. Its strongest spatial references are repeated extensively, while red styling, category-lighting distinctions and room-archetype coverage remain inconsistent. All rules, examples and approval language remain draft proposals—not evidence of adoption, product efficacy or quality approval.
Findings: The proposed spatial language is clearest in the repeatedly used cream-and-olive bedroom. A low horizontal bed, tall left opening, sheer curtain, textured wall, woven-looking rug and leaf shadows work together. Borrow this relationship between architecture and light, not the reference bed or its exact décor. [V008, V017, V018, V023, V029, V031]
The draft's restoration narrative broadly aligns with the supplied positioning, but the images illustrate mood rather than efficacy. Everyday pause, supportive presence and renewed readiness are compatible with 'Motivating Reset.' Neither resting poses nor calm rooms prove stress mitigation, physical recovery or a dramatic transformation. [P028, P055, P056, P057, V004, V008, V009, V010]
Category breadth can coexist with a shared environment without recolouring products. Blue mattresses, green beds, teal and mustard sofas, and beige recliners retain distinct appearances against predominantly warm, quiet surroundings. The room should adapt to the exact SKU; category palette descriptions should not override it. [V003, V007, V019, V020, V032, V034, V037]
Supported contact is more useful than generic smiling as a human-direction cue. Visible examples include legs on an extended footrest, feet placed in a floor device, bodies resting on mattresses and heads supported by pillows. Books, mugs and companionship supply modest lived activity without requiring presenter gestures. [V002, V004, V006, V009, V027]
Red is consistently proposed as identification, but the illustrated environmental boundary is unresolved. The crowded red room is clearly negative, yet ostensibly calmer examples still use red cushions, throws, runners, art and furniture. The later prohibition on red bedding and props needs reconciliation with these draft examples. [V015, V016, V025, V035, V128]
The nature references demonstrate framed greenery more convincingly than a strict one-plant approach. Large openings and leaf shadows create an architectural relationship with nature. Several lounge, niche and bedside examples nevertheless scatter smaller pots across shelves and tables; one coherent green zone would express the stated hierarchy more clearly. [V012, V021, V029, V030]
Morning, neutral-day and evening modes are not yet separated reliably by the chosen examples. The same sunlit lounge and bedroom recur across different purposes, while the evening page includes bright sky and daylight. Distinct lighting references are needed if these modes are to become reproducible production directions. [V021, V031, V032, V033, V034]
Product-detail imagery supplies a useful complement to room atmosphere. Visible weave, upholstery curvature, fabric drape and exposed motion hardware offer concrete subjects for close shots. They can explain appearance and construction without substantiating fibre identity, breathability, skin safety or mechanical performance. [V020, V026, V027, V028]
Rendered typography and logo treatments are not consistent enough to serve as final identity specifications. The opening pages use serif deck text; the identity inset shows an uppercase symbol/wordmark and sans-serif messaging; later pages display a lowercase serif Duroflex rendering. Font substitution and draft assembly must be resolved against authoritative artwork. [V001, V002, V007, V010]
The same small reference library carries many different arguments. Repeated bedrooms, the arched niche, cream lounge and lamp-lit corner establish consistency, but repetition is not independent evidence of broad applicability across homes, products, lighting conditions or channels. [V008, V011, V012, V018, V023, V025, V028, V036]
The four-room menu has uneven visual coverage. Bedroom and lounge settings are well represented, and V004 offers a domestic device-use example. A clearly planned recovery corner and a credible Retail Calm Zone are not demonstrated; contact sheets and decorative wall vignettes do not fill that gap. [V004, V021, V024, V037]
Photographic breathing space must be distinguished from page-layout whitespace. Real walls, openings and floor area can support product hierarchy. Ivory slide margins and bordered insets cannot demonstrate the proposed in-scene space ratio, nor justify adding artificial contrast patches or fades. [V001, V017, V019, V038]
Highly themed settings require stronger adaptation than the neutral domestic references. Forest staging, a strongly gridded-screen room and flower-framed seaside arches are more literal and theatrical than the proposed everyday contemporary home. Borrow openness, filtered light or sheltered seating—not destination-wellness luxury or complete stylistic sets. [P028, V005, V006, V013, V018, V021, V034]
Conflicts: V006 depicts red shorts, while V009, V015 and V035 include red bedding or props; supplied V128 explicitly lists red outfits, bedding and props as DON'Ts. These draft examples need reconciliation, not automatic approval. | V030 asks for one substantial plant or architectural greenery, but its lounge and bedside examples distribute several smaller plants across niches, tables and furniture. | V034's evening description specifies low warm light and wine/olive/walnut, yet its prominent examples include teal and mustard products, bright exterior sky and a sunlit lounge. Resolve the reference selection without recolouring the products. | V021 names four room archetypes but presents five loosely mapped images, none clearly demonstrating retail circulation, display planning or a Retail Calm Zone. | V013 advises borrowing rather than copying styles, while V006 and V021 use strongly themed architectural settings. This is a tension in literalness, not evidence that a geographic origin can be inferred from the images. | V038 states a photographic breathing-space target, but much of its apparent openness is slide-layout margin. The proposed ratio is not demonstrated within the room images.
Gaps: Only V001–V038 were visually reviewed in this batch. Other supplied guide passages are textual context; the remaining pages of the 151-slide draft were not visually assessed here. | Final logo artwork, authoritative typography and adopted graphic specifications are absent. PPTX font substitution may explain some rendered differences. | No verified SKU asset pack establishes exact colour, fabric, branding, dimensions or construction for the reference products. Scene imagery may be synthetic, and material names cannot be authenticated from pixels. | The supplied May 2025 positioning provides strategy, not exact-product efficacy substantiation. No health, airflow, recovery or skin-safety claims can be certified from this batch. | Embedded campaigns and contact sheets do not constitute a dated public-site or social audit. Their offers, product names and graphic treatments are not permanent brand rules. | Distinct production examples are needed for retail, recovery-device settings, ordinary room scales and clearly differentiated morning/day/evening lighting. | Still images cannot verify motion clearance, mechanism operation, complete anatomy or sustained body-product contact. No videos were reviewed. | No measured crop tests, recognition studies, adoption decisions or completed approval records establish that the proposed visual signature or breathing-space rule has been validated.

supplied-draft-visual-guide-2
Coverage: V039, V040, V041, V042, V043, V044, V045, V046, V047, V048, V049, V050, V051, V052, V053, V054, V055, V056, V057, V058, V059, V060, V061, V062, V063, V064, V065, V066, V067, V068, V069, V070, V071, V072, V073, V074, V075, V076
Reviewed all 38 images, V039–V076. This draft develops Duroflex through warm architectural settings, tactile surfaces, everyday resting gestures and a proposed four-part asset system. Its strongest visual mechanisms are directional daylight, restrained object placement and visible product–body contact. Repeated imagery also reveals unresolved red usage, scenic settings that strain the domestic brief, and examples that do not fully demonstrate their stated shot classes. All guidance remains draft art direction—not adoption, quality approval or product-efficacy evidence. Rendered typography, illustrative rooms and human scenes require source-level verification before production.
Findings: Architectural negative space is more convincing than merely increasing slide whitespace. The recurring terrace bedroom reserves a broad wall above a low bed and readable floor beside it. Borrow that physical arrangement and side-light logic for copy placement; the cream slide canvas does not justify adding white patches, haze, blur masks or fades to a photograph. [V039, V041, V046, V068]
The tactile vocabulary connects room surfaces, clothing and product details. Creased clothing, rumpled bedding, ribbed walls and upholstery macros express attentive, human-scale warmth consistent with the supplied empathy strategy. Their role is sensory communication, not verification of fibre content, construction quality or technical benefit. [V040, V042, V058, V059, V076, P054]
The niche reference supports organised domestic zoning, but not a completed retail concept. Recessed shelves and a floating cabinet repeatedly contain objects while preserving foreground floor. This is useful for restrained bedroom, living and retail display zones, but requires adaptation for actual product testing, access, signage and circulation. [V042, V044, V045, V046]
Three different rejection arguments rely on the same exaggerated room. Clutter, saturated red, reflective surfaces, formal presentation clothing and expansive gestures occur together. The example makes their combined effect clear, but cannot isolate which factor causes distrust or justify rejecting every campaign visible in the neighbouring contact sheets. [V043, V054, V061]
Product-supported activity is the recurring human grammar. Reading, cup-holding, head support and shared shoulder contact translate the dependable-companion strategy into observable actions. Preserve those actions and support relationships without treating appearance as evidence of nationality, authentic relationships, candidness or emotional outcomes. [V047, V048, V049, V050, V053, V055, V056, V062, P055]
The proposed reset arc is illust

rated through endpoints, not demonstrated as a sequence. Stretching and reclining recur, but there is no continuous contracted-to-ready performance or clear re-entry into everyday activity. A future sequence could express the strategic motivating reset through modest actions, without implying dramatic transformation or product-caused recovery. [V051, V052, V057, V067, P028]
Wardrobe coordination should not become product recolouring. Muted garments coexist with navy, mustard, green and cream products. This supports adapting clothing, architecture and accessories around the exact SKU, rather than forcing every product into the wardrobe palette or assuming similar-looking textiles share a composition. [V058, V059, V060, V066, V071]
Red is restrained in the page template but inconsistent inside positive references. The outer slides generally use red for the wordmark and headline emphasis, while repeated positive bedrooms contain red runners, cushions and benches. Human boards also use red objects and wine clothing. These examples require reconciliation with the draft no-red-bedding, props and outfits language; they are not permissions to override scene policy. [V039, V041, V042, V048, V050, V068, V074, V128]
The four shot classes are useful planning categories, but their examples overlap. The isolated navy sofa clearly demonstrates Icon, room views demonstrate World, and mattress edges suggest Intelligence. Yet Icon includes room scenes, Inhabited Hero includes empty furniture, and the pillow page lacks a clear pillow hero. A production matrix needs distinct, verified deliverables rather than assuming the montage satisfies all classes. [V063, V064, V065, V066, V067, V068, V069, V075, V076]
Category mood can change through light and use while retaining a shared environment. Bedroom examples favour bright pale surfaces and ordered bed framing; living examples introduce deeper upholstery, warmer light and articulation details. Shared tactile backgrounds and restrained layouts can connect them, provided the room adapts to the product rather than imposing a different category identity. [V070, V071, V074, V075, V076, V095, V108]
Airboost and Duropedic are not visually differentiated by the principal room photographs. The same two blue-white mattress scenes serve both pages. The distinction is mainly in the stated proposition and supporting tiles. Fresh colour, resting poses and a lifted layer cannot establish airflow, pressure relief or orthopaedic performance; exact-product documentation and substantiation remain necessary. [V072, V073, V069, P053]
Some scenic examples pull away from the proposed grounded-home world. The recurring flower-framed arch, dramatic scenic opening and sea-facing bed can read as destination or set-piece imagery. Borrow product visibility and framed depth, but adapt the architecture into a believable home rather than copying the entire escapist setting. [V051, V052, V057, V062, V067, V071, V074, V018]
The rendered deck has a consistent editorial hierarchy with a separate divider treatment. Most pages use a cream ground, upper-left red Duroflex wordmark, small section label, large black/red serif title and right-side imagery. Black dividers switch to bold white titles and small red labels. Embedded boards are sometimes cropped; none of this establishes exact fonts, colour codes or final logo-layout specifications. [V039, V047, V048, V063, V064, V069]
Conflicts: V039, V042, V050, V068 and V074 present red runners, cushions and benches as positive references, while V128 explicitly rejects red bedding and props. Exact product colour must remain intact; decorative examples need reconciliation rather than automatic adoption. | V066 states “pure product” for Icon but includes furnished rooms and a macro detail. The isolated sofa fits the proposition more directly than the entire collage. | V067 calls for an Inhabited Hero yet includes an empty recliner and unoccupied sofa references. These cannot independently demonstrate human interaction. | V071 proposes warm social settings, but its prominent examples are an isolated sofa, texture crops and an empty scenic recliner. The stated social dimension is weakly depicted. | V074 asks for beds integrated with bedding, while its dominant green-bed image exposes a bare mattress. Architectural anchoring is demonstrated more clearly than bedding integration. | The scenic arch recliner repeated in V051, V052, V057, V062, V067 and V071 creates tension with V018’s contemporary-home, non-showroom proposition. Its value as inspiration does not make the whole setting suitable. | V047 visibly uses lustrous wine-coloured sleepwear, whereas V058–V061 emphasise matte, natural-looking restraint. The intended allowance for sheen needs clarification; the image does not establish synthetic composition.
Gaps: No adoption record or final approval accompanies this batch. Draft labels such as “approved,” “mandatory” and “human approval” do not change the guide’s provisional status. | Exact-SKU source photography, verified dimensions, fabric specifications, construction drawings and component compatibility are needed before these references can govern production. | No exact-product substantiation is supplied here for airflow, pressure relief, orthopaedic support, neck ease, recovery or stress-release claims. May 2025 positioning remains strategy, not efficacy proof. | Repeated and small collages limit inspection of fingers, limb continuity, seat compression, pillow deformation, product labels and contact shadows. Original-resolution assets require individual technical review. | The life-stage and relationship propositions lack clearly demonstrated parent–child or broader family interactions. Nationality, relationships and real-world authenticity cannot be established from these portraits. | Movement is represented only through saved stills. Transition speed, mechanism operation and continuity have not been reviewed in video. | The retail page supplies no store plan or operational evidence. Embedded campaign contact sheets are not a current website audit and do not establish permanent campaign, offer or product rules. | Reference provenance, real material composition and architectural origins remain unverified. Source font and logo assets are also needed because rendering may substitute typography and embedded boards are sometimes cropped.

supplied-draft-visual-guide-3
Coverage: V077, V078, V079, V080, V081, V082, V083, V084, V085, V086, V087, V088, V089, V090, V091, V092, V093, V094, V095, V096, V097, V098, V099, V100, V101, V102, V103, V104, V105, V106, V107, V108, V109, V110, V111, V112, V113, V114
Reviewed all 38 images, V077–V114, individually. This draft batch develops product presentation, graphic hierarchy, category moods and activation through repeated room references, people boards and small asset contact sheets. Its strongest visual continuity is warm neutral architecture, directional daylight, tactile surfaces and prominent products. Several propositions are not demonstrated by their accompanying examples, particularly typography, restrained red, massage use, iconography and detail proof. All guidance and examples remain draft—not evidence of adoption, quality approval, exact-SKU accuracy or efficacy. Embedded contact sheets are not an independently dated website audit.
Findings: Warm domestic continuity is carried by architecture and light more than by a fixed product palette. Recessed niches, slatted surfaces, pale textured walls, planted edges and side light recur across bedrooms, living rooms and architectural crops. These are useful transferable relationships; exact materials and origins remain unverified. [V079, V081, V106, V107, V111]
The motion references provide a usable progression from silhouette to detail to room use. The repeated teal sofa, mustard footrest macro and skylit grey-sofa room cover distinct viewing needs. The strongest spatial lesson is preserving foreground extension space while keeping tables off-axis—not treating exposed linkage as the entire lifestyle story. [V077, V099, V100, V112]
The production checklist expands the draft shot classes into communication deliverables. Icon, Inhabited Hero, World and Intelligence can organize the later hero/detail/human/use-case/technology/ecommerce/sale list. A mapping is still needed so one thumbnail is not mistaken for completed coverage across several requirements. [V065, V082, V112, V114]
Category distinction is strongest for sleep and seating, but underdeveloped for recovery and accessories. Blue mattress surfaces and airy rooms contrast with deeper seating colours and tactile motion details. Recovery repeatedly relies on the same recliner and generic resting people; accessories rely on props rather than identifiable accessory heroes. [V083, V095, V096, V099, V102, V105]
Rendered typography does not consistently demonstrate the stated sans-serif direction. Large serif headings, serif body copy, red emphasis and cream margins form the visible slide hierarchy. The intended type system must be checked against source assets because rendering substitution could explain the discrepancy. [V084, V086, V109]
The red examples require reconciliation with the draft’s own restraint language. Runner, cushions, bench, artwork and graphic bars create multiple red cues, whereas the supplied guardrail discourages red bedding and props. Preserve genuine SKU red details; do not treat the illustrated room styling as permission to add red throughout a scene. [V084, V087, V088, V113, V128]
The same overloaded room functions ambiguously on the intensity page and clearly as a negative elsewhere. Its dense red décor, starburst, reflective clutter and presenter gestures should not become a sale-level template. Later negative headings clarify that greater promotional volume is not equivalent to greater environmental saturation. [V088, V093, V098, V101, V104]
Graphic propositions are often accompanied by moodboards rather than operational examples. Logo restraint, rounded containment, icons, single-message hierarchy and digital CTA clarity lack enlarged specifications or finished comparative layouts. Cropped inset logos and tiny symbols cannot establish production standards. [V085, V089, V091, V092, V113]
Natural illumination and graphic atmosphere must remain separate concepts. The olive bedroom provides actual wall space, window falloff and leaf shadows. Pale layout strips and the gradient proposition do not authorize fading or masking a photograph to manufacture copy contrast. [V084, V089, V090, V111, V113]
Observable human activity aligns with the supplied companionable positioning without proving a health outcome. Reading, cup-holding, stretching and supported reclining are concrete, ordinary actions consistent with warmth and attentive care. Identity, authenticity, stress reduction and recovery cannot be inferred from styling or expressions. [V081, V106, V114, P055, P057]
Texture and product visibility are useful descriptive evidence, not benefit substantiation. Weave, quilting, labels, cutaway illustrations and relaxed poses can explain appearance or intended use. Claims about airflow, relief, support or recovery still require exact-product evidence beyond the positioning strategy and pixels. [V080, V097, V102, V112, P028, P054]
The coastal-arch recliner is a recurring spatial outlier. Its sea view, pale arch and vivid flowering frame create destination-like scenery, unlike the quieter enclosed homes. Borrow product framing and openness selectively; adapt the setting toward the draft’s contemporary-home intention rather than copying a resort mood. [V078, V079, V083, V100, V102, V103, V114, V013, V018]
Activation intensity is proposed, but not demonstrated through a controlled sequence. Quiet rooms and dense promotional contact sheets establish broad endpoints. They do not show one exact SKU, scene and identity system progressing consistently from brand to product, digital and sal

e. [V082, V088, V110, V111, V112, V113]
Retail calm is supported by architectural inspiration, not by retail implementation evidence. The slatted wall and arched niche offer zoning and surface continuity. Actual cross-category merchandising, customer circulation, product trials and accessibility remain unshown. [V081, V107, V108]
Conflicts: V086 specifies sans-serif hierarchy while its rendered main typography is visibly serif. Font substitution is a possible explanation, not a confirmed resolution. | V087 and V113 call for punctuation or a single red cue, yet their bedroom examples contain several red furnishings, textiles and graphic elements; V128 further discourages red bedding and props. | V088 places an overloaded red room beside the intensity ladder without a clear local negative label, while V093, V098, V101 and V104 reuse it as an explicit warning. | V080 promises fabric, seam, switch and tag detail proof, but its two illustrations are environmental room views rather than dedicated product-detail crops. | V099’s “Evening Exhale” proposition includes a strongly skylit daytime room and neutral studio product view, so the intended time-of-day mood is not consistently depicted. | V102 and V103 describe precise recovery interactions and technology detail, but their prominent images show generic reclining, sleeping and furnished rooms rather than identifiable massage-device contact. | The scenic coastal recliner and repeated “spa-tech” wording risk a luxury-wellness reading if copied literally, whereas P028 excludes deriving the positioning from luxurious wellness experiences.
Gaps: Approved master logo artwork, typography assets, colour specifications, icon families, panel geometry and finished hierarchy templates are not established by these rendered pages. | Exact-SKU reference packs are needed to preserve colour, fabric appearance, labels, construction, controls and motion configuration. The draft pictures do not verify these attributes. | Recovery needs identifiable devices, correct supported interaction and close-up contact views; accessories need clear product heroes rather than mainly surrounding décor. | High-resolution source assets are required to inspect small labels, hands, anatomy, occlusion, product contact and control details. Repeated contact sheets are insufficient for quality approval. | No controlled retouch comparisons, motion sequences or videos are reviewed. Rotation, rocking, extension limits and operational behaviour remain unverified. | No complete responsive digital layout, usable CTA system or same-scene activation ladder is demonstrated. | Retail floor plans, measured clearances, accessibility provisions and cross-category display trials are absent. | The embedded campaign sheets lack sufficient provenance and collection-date context for an independent current-website comparison. Visible offers and named campaigns must remain contextual examples. | Reference authenticity, material composition, dimensions and origins are unverified; some imagery may be synthetic. Positioning and draft art direction provide no exact-product efficacy substantiation.

supplied-draft-visual-guide-4
Coverage: V115, V116, V117, V118, V119, V120, V121, V122, V123, V124, V125, V126, V127, V128, V129, V130, V131, V132, V133, V134, V135, V136, V137, V138, V139, V140, V141, V142, V143, V144, V145, V146, V147, V148, V149, V150, V151
Reviewed all 37 images, V115–V151. This draft batch develops channel applications, room/people/red guardrails, human-rendering studies, character references and production checklists. Strong recurring cues are warm architectural space, product-first framing, tactile detail and supported everyday activity. Important unresolved issues include contradictory red examples, fashion-oriented character poses, incomplete channel demonstrations and an inconsistent scorecard. All rules and ‘locked’ characters remain draft proposals—not evidence of adoption, product efficacy or quality approval.
Findings: The main guide template uses red selectively, while the character appendix uses a different graphic language. Cream pages repeat a red wordmark, black/red serif headlines and small metadata. The appendix switches to black dividers, handwritten boards, photo grids and unbranded studio triptychs. These reference-board treatments should not be mistaken for a resolved public-facing Duroflex identity system. [V115, V124, V148, V151, V130, V136, V137, V144]
Architectural calm is most convincingly demonstrated through openings, floor area and layered low-contrast surfaces. Screen-like glazing or garden openings provide directional light; rugs and low platforms anchor products; olive, cream and wood-toned layers avoid visual flatness. Borrow those spatial relationships, adapting the room to the exact SKU rather than recolouring the product or adding artificial contrast patches. [V116, V119, V125]
Repeated assets demonstrate a proposed reusable image library, not separate channel executions. The frontal blue-edged mattress, isolated teal loveseat and red-accented bedrooms recur across PDP, performance and launch propositions. This supports reusable room, icon and detail coverage, but does not demonstrate working interfaces, CTA placement, proof modules or completed campaign adaptations. [V116, V120, V123, V150]
The role of the crowded red room becomes explicit only in the guardrails sequence. Earlier application collages mix the saturated room with quieter examples without clear labels. Later pages consistently place it under DON’T. Its ornate styling, presentation gestures and red saturation should therefore be read as a negative comparator, not spatial inspiration to reproduce. [V117, V121, V125, V126, V127, V128]
The proposed red principle is clearer than its affirmative examples. The text advocates controlled punctuation, yet positive-looking examples combine red bedding, cushions, benches, mugs, books or clothing. Graphic red, authentic product details and optional room accents need separate definitions before production; the examples do not override exact-SKU preservation. [V120, V121, V124, V128]
Domestic activity references and character-presentation references serve different purposes. Reading, pillow contact and supported reclining show how people might inhabit products. Casting boards prioritise direct gaze, garment display, athletic settings or posed stance. Borrow appearance continuity and surface detail from the latter, but re-stage activity rather than transferring fashion poses directly into inhabited heroes. [V122, V126, V127, V138, V142, V144, V147]
The human-rendering studies provide a coherent contact-and-surface checklist. Across these pages, pores through highlights, hair density, non-identical fingers, pressure, seams and force-related folds recur. Applied together, these checks can support believable product/person interaction. Added skin texture alone cannot repair unsupported weight, incorrect anatomy or inconsistent light. [V131, V132, V133, V134, V135, V149]
Scenic recliner imagery sits uneasily beside the more credible domestic bedroom language. The flowering arch and distant scenic view offer a more escapist setting than garden-connected, warm modern bedrooms. Borrow the recliner’s clear silhouette if useful, but adapt the setting toward ordinary home restoration rather than importing resort-style wellness or copying a regional aesthetic. [V115, V116, V123, V125, V013, V018, P028]
Visual proof and product efficacy remain distinct throughout the batch. Clean product views and simplified technical communication align with the supplied preference for thoughtful innovation and no overpromising. Neither attractive rooms, exposed layers nor relaxed people establish stress-release, pain-relief or other exact-product outcomes. [V116, V123, V129, P028, P054, P057]
Movement is proposed through poses and sequences, but no motion execution is available. Stretching, hair movement and walking sequences suggest changes in body state. They cannot establish transition speed, continuity, believable inertia or the absence of frantic editing. Motion evaluation requires the actual clips. [V115, V135, V141]
The six-item delivery list can extend the earlier four-class shoot system, but its mapping is unstated. World, Inhabited Hero and Icon have close equivalents; Details could supply Intelligence assets, while Performance and Sale appear to be channel derivatives. Clarifying that mapping would prevent duplicate deliverables and distinguish source photography from graphic adaptations. [V065, V120, V150]
Conflicts: V128 prohibits red bedding and props while its DO image includes a red bed runner, cushion and bench. V124 additionally presents red mugs, a book and burgundy clothing within its positive human board. | V126’s activity-led, non-performing proposition contrasts with the fashion poses in V144–V147. These may be useful casting studies, but their inclusion does not resolve suitability for consumer-facing inhabited scenes. | V127 emphasises quiet homewear and rejects branded athleisure and synthetic shine; V142 explicitly proposes athleisure, while V143 depicts lustrous pyjamas. This requires a styling clarification, not an inference that the garments are branded or made from synthetic fibres. | V151 states a 100-point score but lists only eight 10-point criteria. Its pass/refine thresholds cannot be used consistently without correcting the scoring structure. | V130 reintroduces PART V and footer page 17 inside the surrounding PART VIII sequence; V136 then says ‘Locked Characters’. This editorial assembly does not establish formal locking or approval. | V149’s suggestion to reduce distracting labels is too broad for exact-product imagery: authentic product branding must remain preserved under the client scene policy.
Gaps: Exact-SKU source assets, verified construction details, colour/fabric references and approved branding files are not supplied here. Rendered deck typography may also contain font substitutions. | V118 does not show a storefront; V119 does not show a complete retail layout; V116–V121 do not demonstrate usable PDP, marketplace or advertising interfaces. No current-site comparison can be established from these draft collages. | V129 lacks a positive science example. Technical details and any efficacy language need product-specific substantiation beyond the May 2025 positioning. | Reference authenticity, actual material composition, dimensions, camera/film provenance and printed character identities remain unverified. ‘Locked’ does not establish adoption or quality approval. | Only stills are available. Motion pacing, body transitions, mechanism movement and temporal consistency remain unreviewed. | The prompt toolkit omits operational requirements for exact-product preservation, architectural negative space, coherent shadows/occlusion/contact and supported anatomy; these need explicit production controls. | The scorecard needs its missing 20 points or a revised denominator, and the four-class/six-deliverable asset taxonomy needs reconciliation before production use. | Many embedded contact-sheet captions and product labels are too small for dependable detailed reading; their presence does not verify named products, offers or claims.

supplied-positioning-1
Coverage: P001, P002, P003, P004, P005, P006, P007, P008, P009, P010, P011, P012, P013, P014, P015, P016, P017, P018, P019, P020, P021, P022, P023, P024, P025, P026, P027, P028, P029, P030, P031, P032, P033, P034, P035, P036, P037, P038
Reviewed all 38 supplied images, P001–P038. The May 2025 presentation develops Duroflex’s proposed shift from basic mattress functionality toward “Motivating Reset,” connecting everyday strain with restoration and renewed participation in life. Its photographs illustrate audience tensions; its cross-category examples demonstrate communication mechanisms, not Duroflex art direction. Red presentation graphics are not room-palette instructions. Posit

ioning statements do not establish exact-SKU efficacy, and the supplied Visual World Guide remains a draft blueprint rather than evidence of adoption or approval.
Findings: The strategic progression is from familiar functionality to a specific role in everyday life. Early pages diagnose disconnected technology stories; later pages propose renewal and stress relevance.
